title: SRS Review AI — wire contract
description: Single source of truth for the JSON exchanged between the Flutter app and the FastAPI proxy. Both sides are tested against contracts/fixtures/*.json. Bump x-contract-version on any breaking change and update both sides in the same PR.

IssueType.description: Quality issue vocabulary for the LLM (ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 flavoured). Deterministic rule checks use $defs/CheckId instead — do not mix the two vocabularies. This is the defect CLASS, not the criterion the model was judging: an editable criterion is an id from the criteria list and travels in Issue.criterion_id. `other` is the vocabulary's escape hatch — the server maps any unrecognised value to it rather than failing the unit, because the app rejects an unknown type loudly and a verified finding must not die over a label.

Verification.description: Result of server-side quote verification. 'rejected' issues are DROPPED by the server and never reach the app, so the app only ever sees exact|fuzzy.

CheckId.description: Deterministic (rule-based, offline, zero-token) checks derived from the SEP490 syllabus and from review-rules/RULEBOOK.md. M2 reference checks (duplicate_ids, missing_postcondition) extend the same enum — they share the on-wire shape but live in a separate UI section. This list had drifted behind the Dart CheckId enum; it is now complete as of rubric v3, and adding a CheckId without adding it here is the drift to watch for.

criterion_id.description: Id of the evaluation criterion this issue answers, when the model named one — a row from the (editable) criteria list the prompt carried. This is what makes an edited or user-added criterion traceable in the findings; null when the model named none. Additive: an older reader ignores it.

quote.description: Verbatim excerpt from the requirement text. Verified server-side before being returned.

similarity.description: Fuzzy-match ratio; null when verification == exact.

context_note.description: Free-text observation about diagrams/images on the requirement's page. NEVER contributes to score (research 10, Risks).

dropped_issue_count.description: Issues the LLM produced whose quote failed verification and were dropped. Surfaced in the UI as the anti-hallucination metric.

prompt_tokens.description: Tokens consumed by the prompt in upstream LLM call.

BatchUnitResult.description: One unit's outcome inside a /review/batch response, addressed by its index in the request's `units` array. Position in the array is NOT the contract: a unit that fails drops out of `results` and lands in `failed`, so a client that zipped by position would attribute scores to the wrong requirement.

BatchUnitFailure.description: A unit the server could not review. The message is provider-neutral (the proxy never forwards a raw provider error) and is shown to the user.

BatchReviewResponse.description: Answer to POST /review/batch. Always 200 when the request itself was acceptable: the units that WERE reviewed are cached and already paid for, so a 502 would make the client throw them away. Batching is a cost optimisation only — every quote in every result is still verified against that unit's own text.

grounded.description: false => the answer was not supported by the document; the app shows the 'not found in document' state (AC5).

DeterministicFinding.description: Produced client-side (Dart) — no network, no tokens. See docs/rubric.md F7/F8/F9.

subject.description: Which UC/requirement the finding is about; null for document-level findings such as uc_count.
